(owner as per Transport Authority) ........ Registered Owner/ Respondent no.2 Mact No:992/19 Amar Singh v. Vijender @ Kale P.No. 1 Of 19 Bk 3. Abhishek Gupta S/o Sh. texts.facts: The present accident claim is based on a detailed accident report (DAR) filed by the police in terms of provisions of MV Act. In fact four connected DARs were filed in respect of same accident in which one Amar Singh suffered injury while one Ram Singh, Ashok and Dev Raj sustained fatal injuries and died. Amar Singh ( Dar) vs Vijender (88/19, Nfc) on 29 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/182501694/ 1 2. The brief facts of the case are that on 19.04.2019, on receiving GD No.4A &5A regarding accident, ASI Manoj Kumar alongwith HC Sanjeev reached at the spot i.e. CRRI red light, Mathura Road, New Delhi where an Auto No.DL1RV-1499 was found in accidental condition and injured persons were informed to have been taken to Apollo hospital. On reaching the hospital, he came to know that three of the injured namely Dev Raj S/o Rampal, Ashok S/o Ram Swaroop and Ram Singh S/o Puran Singh died in the hospital while injured/petitioner Amar Singh S/o Puran Singh was found admitted under treatment. Injured Amar Singh stated that he used to work as halwai in marriage MACT NO:992/19 Amar Singh v. Vijender @ Kale P.No. 2 Of 19 BK parties. In the intervening night of 18.04.2019 &19.04.2019 at about 12.15 AM, he was returning from work in a hired Auto bearing no. DL-1RV-1499(hereinafter referred to as offending vehicle) from Jaitpur to Nehru Nagar. At that time Ram Singh (since deceased) occupied the front seat next to the driver and injured/petitioner Amar Singh, Ashok (since deceased) and Devraj (since deceased) occupied the seat behind the driver. The driver of the offending auto was driving it rashly and negligently. At around 1 AM when they reached Mathura Road, Respondent no.1 while continuing to drive the offending vehicle at high speed, tried cleaning the mirror/glass (Sheesha) of the auto, due to which the auto got dis-balanced and fell on the other side of the road. Due to the accident, the passengers in the auto sustained severe injuries on their head. They were taken to the hospital where Ram Singh, Ashok and Devraj died during treatment. Petitioner Amar Singh was discharge after treatment. 3. An FIR no.88/2019 dated 19.04.2019 was registered u/s 279,337,304 A IPC & 3/181 MV Act at PS New Friends Colony and the matter was investigated. After investigation, charge sheet was filed before concerned criminal court against the driver of the offending vehicle while DAR was filed before this Tribunal. 4. Respondent no.1 is driver of offending vehicle, Respondent no.2 is the registered owner and Respondent no.3 is the possession holder of the offending vehicle. Offending vehicle is uninsured. 5. In response to the DAR, Respondent no.2 Dharmender filed his reply. No reply filed by Respondent no.1 and 3 despite opportunity. MACT NO:992/19 Amar Singh v. Vijender @ Kale P.No. 3 Of 19 BK In written statement filed by Respondent no.2, it is pleaded that Respondent no.2/Dharmender is neither the driver nor the owner of the offending vehicle. It is stated that Respondent no.2 had sold the offending vehicle to Respondent no.3/Abhishek Gupta. It is pleaded that Respondent no.3 had also executed an affidavit of purchase in favour of Respondent no.2, in his own hand-writing while a Form No.29 & Form No.30 were executed by Respondent no.2 showing transfer of the offending vehicle on 07.03.2019 i.e. prior to the date of accident. 6. On the basis of pleadings on record, following issues were framed on 21.10.2020. OPP. Amar Singh ( Dar) vs Vijender (88/19, Nfc) on 29 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/182501694/ 2 2. OPP. 3. Relief. 7. Petitioner Amar Singh examined himself as PW-1 and led his evidence by way of affidavit as Ex.PW1/A. As per the affidavit, on 19.04.2019 at about 1:00 AM, he was travelling in TSR bearing registration no.DL-1RV-1499 and going to Nehru Nagar from Jaitpur. The said offending vehicle was being driven by Respondent no.1/Vijender @Kale in rash and negligent manner and when said TSR reached at CRRI Red light, Mathura Road, New Delhi, all of sudden said TSR turned turtle, due to which he sustained injuries. He was taken to Apollo hospital and declared injuries on his head, spine and all over the body. He MACT NO:992/19 Amar Singh v. Vijender @ Kale P.No . 4 Of 19 BK was also treated by some private doctors at his native place i.e. Rampur, U.P. and remained under treatment for four months. He was 26 years of age at the time of accident. His date of birth is 10.10.1993. He was doing work of catering at Delhi and was earning Rs.18,000/- per month. He was unable to do his work for about four months. He spent Rs.1 lac on his treatment, special diet, conveyance and other expenses. He relied upon his Aadhar card as Ex. PW-1/1, MLC as Ex.PW-1/2 and DAR as Ex.PW-1/3. He was not cross-examined by any of the respondents. No other witness was examined on behalf of petitioner. Respondents did not lead any evidence. 8. Final arguments in details were addressed on behalf of the petitioner.
texts.arguments: Even the defence of Respondent no.2 as to disowning his liability on account of transfer of the offending vehicle to Amar Singh ( Dar) vs Vijender (88/19, Nfc) on 29 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/182501694/ 3 Thus, it stands proved that the petitioner suffered injuries in road traffic accident due to rash and negligence of Respondent no.1. 12.
